<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 118|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XII.}}</noinclude>you vvil not forgiue, neither vvil your father that is in heauen, forgiue you your sinnes. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=27}}† And they come againe to Hierusalem.

And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21. 23. Lu. 20, 2.''}}* vvhen he vvalked in the temple, there come to him the cheefe Priestes and the Scribes and the Auncients, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=28}}† and they say to him, In vvhat povver doest thou these things? and vvho hath giuen thee this povver, that thou shouldest doe these things? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=29}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering said to them, I also vvil aske you one vvord, and ansvver you me: and I vvil tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=30}}† The baptisme of Iohn vvas it from heauen, or from men? ansvver me. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=31}}† But they thought vvith them selues, saying, If vve say, From heauen: he vvil say, VVhy then did you not beleeue him? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=32}}† If vve say, From men, they feared the people. for al accounted Iohn that he vvas in deede a Prophet. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=33}}† And they ansvvering say to {{sc|Iesvs}}, VVe knovv not. And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering saith to them, Neither do I tel you in vvhat povver I doe these things.

{{c|{{larger|A N N O T A T I O N S}}}}
{{c|{{sc|Chap. XI.}}}}

''16. Vessel through the temple.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Profaning of Gods Church.}}He could not abide to see the Temple of God profaned, no nor suffred those things to be done in it, which otherwise were not vnlawful but honest, if they had been done in dewe place. How much lesse can he abide the profaning of Churches now with Heretical seruice and preaching of heresie and blasphemie?

''17. Denne of theeues.''] If the Temple was then a denne of theeues, because of profane and secular merchandise: how much more now, when the house appointed for the Holy Sacrifice and Sacrament of the Bodie of Christ, is made a denne for the Ministers of Caluins bread?

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XII.}}}}}}

{{c|''He foretelleth to the Iewes in a parable their reprobation most worthy, and the vocation of the Church of the Gentils in their place, 10 him self being the headstone thereof. 13 He defeateth the snare of the Pharisees and Herodians, about paying tribute to Cæsar: 18 answereth also the inuention of the Sadducees against the Resurrection: 28 also the opposition of a Scribe. 35 And so hauing put al the busie sectes to silence, he turneth and poseth them on the other side, because they imagined Christ should be no more but a man. 38 Bidding the people to beware of the Scribes, being ambitious and hypocrites. 41 He commendeth the poore widovv for her two mites, aboue al.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=12|verse=1}}}}ND he began to speake to them in parables, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This man, is God the Father. This vineyard, is (as Esay saith 5, 1.) the house of Israel. The seruants sent, are Moyses and the Prophets, whom the Iewes did diuersely afflict and persecute.}}∷ A man planted a vineyard and made a hedge about it, and digged a trough, and built a tovvre, and let it out to husbandmen: and vvent forth into a strange countrie.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Esa. 5, 1. Mt. 21, 33. Lu. 20, 9.''}} {{verse|chapter=12|verse=2}}† And he sent to the husbandmen in season a seruant, to<noinclude>{{rh|||receiue}}</noinclude>
